body_md:
### 🏟️ Who else is coming to this event?

When more than one bleacher is booked into the same event, the **PICKUP** and **DROP-OFF** headings on your trip card turn into a tappable button. Tap one to see every bleacher due at that event and what its driver is doing right now — **Not Started**, **Picking up Bleacher**, **On Its Way!**, **Arrived** or **Delivered** — and how long ago that changed.

- A bleacher that is **On Its Way!** shows a live countdown, like **ETA: 5h 32m**.
- Pickup and drop-off each have their own list, because the bleachers you collect with are not always the ones you deliver alongside.
- The list works with **no signal**, like the rest of the app.

### 📍 Track a bleacher

Bleachers with a GPS tracker have a **Track** button in that list. It opens a map right inside the app, with **Last Updated** at the top so you know how fresh the pin is. It refreshes every 30 seconds while open, and **Open in Maps** gets you directions. Tracking needs a connection.

### 🔧 Keeping sync healthy behind the scenes

After it finishes syncing, the app now quietly tells our developers how much data your phone is keeping in sync — at most once every few hours. That lets us spot a phone that is getting close to its sync limit and fix it **before** you ever see the **poor connection** screen.

- Nothing changes on your screens, and there is nothing to tap.
- It works with **no signal** too: the note waits on your phone and goes out the next time you are online.

### 🔧 Faster sync for drivers with a long trip history

Drivers with many past trips could get stuck on the **poor connection** screen after signing in — the app was downloading every detail of every trip they had ever done. Now it only keeps the full details of the trips you are working on.

**Trip History** still shows the pickup and drop-off address, the pay breakdown and both inspections for every finished trip, even with no signal. If the office corrects your pay or an address after a trip is done, the change shows up there too.

### 🔑 Signing in for the first time

The **sign-in screen** now has a **First time here?** card for new drivers. You can't create an account in the app — your Account Manager sets it up and emails you an invitation. Tap the card to see the three steps:

- Find the email **Invitation to join Bleacher Rentals** — check your Spam folder too.
- Tap **Accept invitation**, enter your name and create a password.
- Come back to the app and sign in with that same email and password.

Used **Google** or **Apple** when you accepted? Tap the same button on the sign-in screen. No email, or it's more than 30 days old? Ask your Account Manager to send a new one.

Already signed in before? Nothing changes — the card stays folded up out of your way.

### 🔧 Bug Fixes and Performance Improvements

No new screens this time. We tightened up how the Android app is built so it stays fast and healthy on the Play Store — nothing changes about how you use the app.

### 📋 Assets — the whole fleet, in your pocket

A new **Assets** page in the **menu** lists every bleacher the company owns. Search by the number painted on the trailer and open it to read what the office knows about it.

- **Bleacher number, seats, rows, type and opening direction** — what you are looking at.
- **Storage location, zone and total distance** — where it lives and how far you have hauled it.
- **Manufacturer, VIN, tag, hitch type, height, length and GVWR** — the numbers you need at a weigh station or before coupling.
- **Annual inspection** shows at a glance whether it is in date, due soon, or overdue.
- **NVIS and the inspection certificate** open as PDFs when you have signal; the page tells you plainly when you don't.

The whole list and every spec work with **no signal** — it is all on your phone. Assets is read-only: bleacher records stay the office's to maintain, and anything wrong with a bleacher still goes in a damage report.

### 🙅 Turning work down, and handing it back

**You can now decline offered work.** A trip you are offered but cannot take no longer has to be left sitting — decline it and it goes back to the office straight away.

- Already accepted something you can no longer do? **Abandon** it, and the office is told.
- Both show up in **Trip History** alongside your completed work, so your record matches what the office sees.

### 🗓️ Trip History, week by week

**Trip History is now grouped into weeks**, newest first, with **what that week paid** on the week header. The current week is open when you land on the page and older weeks are folded up — tap a week to open it.

Declined and abandoned jobs sit in the same list as your completed work, each marked for what it was. They pay nothing, so they never count toward a week's total.

### 📍 Addresses

Addresses now carry the **country and the exact map pin** the office set, instead of the app guessing from the street line — so maps open on the right spot. Older addresses entered before this change display exactly as they were typed.

### 🚚 What changed

**Damage Reports has a new home.** The old history tab is now a full **Damage Reports** screen with **All** and **Mine** tabs, plus a bleacher filter, so you can see what's already been reported before you file something new.

- Tap **+** to start a report — you'll first see any open reports already on that bleacher, so you're not the third person reporting the same dent.
- See something already reported? Open it and tap **I saw this too** instead of filing a duplicate.
- Fixed something in the field? Open the report and mark it **Fixed** — right from your phone.
- During an inspection, if damage is found, you can now check off an existing open report instead of always starting a new form.

### 🔧 Job types

**Repairs and site visits no longer look like hauls.** Every job now shows what kind of work it is — **Trip**, **Repair / Maintenance**, or **Site Visit / Cleaning / Other** — with its own colour and icon on the trip card, in Trip History and on your upcoming days.

- Repair and site-visit jobs show **one time and one address** instead of a pick up and a drop off, with one set of instructions.
- **No inspection on these jobs.** Nothing is being hauled, so there is nothing to inspect — you tap **Arrived on Site**, do the work, then **Complete Job**.
- Their bill of lading matches: a single **Shipment Information** block, no pick up / drop off columns.
- Times now read the way the office booked them — an exact time, a window like **10:00 AM - 12:00 PM**, or **Any Time**.
- Addresses show in full — street, city, state and ZIP — and open in your maps app at the exact spot when the office pinned one.

### 🆕 What's New — see everything we ship

Open the **menu** (top right) **→ What's New.** Every update to the app now gets
written up here, newest first, so you can see what changed instead of noticing a
button moved.

A blue dot sits on the menu button and on the **What's New** row whenever there
is an update you haven't read yet. Opening the page clears it.

The whole page works with **no signal** — the notes ship inside the app itself,
so you can read them from a yard, a loading dock, or the middle of nowhere.
